name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Seafarer killed on a tanker hit off Qatar on 5 Nov; Iran says two more tankers struck mines in Hormuz
state: A seafarer was killed when the Greek-managed tanker Velos Sapphire was hit by suspected missiles in the Gulf on 5 Nov (gCaptain/Reuters; Times of Israel). Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers struck mines in or near Hormuz on 6 Nov, and the UK navy's agency counted at least 30 attacks on merchant ships in October (CBS News). US escorts are moving some cargoes, but traffic remains materially impeded, meeting the Alert line.
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf faces attacks, mines and higher insurance costs. Mariners should follow UKMTO advisories; consumers may see delays and higher costs on some imported goods.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by attacks and mines (Alert)

sources.title: gCaptain (Reuters) — Seafarer killed in suspected missile attack on tanker in Gulf
Times of Israel — One seafarer killed in missile attack on tanker in Gulf

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
